## Decisions (with @rationale)

- `tile({"factors": [128], "loop": "i"})` :: Tiling i by 128 creates 4 output row-blocks for a 512-row matrix. A 128-row tile fits well in shared memory and gives ea
- `tile({"factors": [128], "loop": "j"})` :: Tiling j by 128 creates 4 output column-blocks. A 128×128 output tile matches the classic cuBLAS-style block size for sq
- `parallel({"mapping": {"i": "threadblock.x"}})` :: Map the tiled i-outer loop to threadblock.x so each SM receives an independent row-block of the output. With 4 i-blocks 
- `parallel({"mapping": {"j": "threadblock.y"}})` :: Map the tiled j-outer loop to threadblock.y to form a 2D grid of (i_blocks × j_blocks) = 4×4 = 16 threadblocks. 2D grid 
- `tile({"loop": "i", "factors": [64]})` :: Tile i by 64 creates 8 row-blocks. Combined with 8 j-blocks (64-tile), we get 64 threadblocks — more than double the 30 
- `tile({"factors": [64], "loop": "j"})` :: Tile j by 64 to match i, completing a 64×64 output block. This symmetric tiling keeps A and B shared memory tiles square
- `parallel({"mapping": {"i": "threadblock.x"}})` :: Map i-outer (8 blocks) to threadblock.x. Combining with j-outer on threadblock.y yields an 8×8 = 64 block grid, ensuring
- `parallel({"mapping": {"j": "threadblock.y"}})` :: Map j-outer (8 blocks) to threadblock.y to complete the 2D 8×8 SM grid. This co-locates blocks that share the same B col
- `vectorize({"loop": "j", "width": 4})` :: Vectorize the j (column) inner loop with width 4 (128-bit loads for fp32). This enables LDG.128 global loads for B's row
